- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to subsequent forecast values.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust quickly; reduce forecast slope downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day horizons; if forecast deviates >3% from 10-day moving average, adjust toward it with 0.5–1.0% per day correction.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates volatility in early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; cap early forecast growth at 1.5–2.0% per day unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.33/1.00 alternation (e.g., 3–5 cycles), model tends to misalign with true price; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast midpoints.
